snippet.title: Interpol: The Trail of Dr. Chaos (PS3) - Full Playthrough
snippet.description:
00:00:00 Intro and San Francisco
00:04:40 New York
00:08:52 Hollywood
00:13:28 Bonus Puzzle 1
00:14:26 St. Petersburg
00:18:13 London
00:21:37 Moscow
00:26:09 Monte Carlo
00:31:29 Tokyo
00:38:56 Paris
00:44:40 Bonus Puzzle 2
00:46:53 Rome
00:54:50 Interpol HQ

Okay. 

So. 

Maybe you can use this as ASMR or something. Like Gemfire. That's been getting viewed a lot recently, and I'm very confused by the traffic, as Gemfire is that quintessential game which is fun as hell to play, but like watching paint dry to observe. But if we are doing this beat-everything-again insanity, this counts too.

Anyway, Interpol: The Trail of Dr. Chaos.

So, when I read this game's description on the old PS3 store, I imagined a Carmen Sandiego-esque detective game. What I got was a home version of PhotoHunt. You know. That digital bar game that was everywhere in the early 2000s? Okay, maybe you don't, but summing up, somebody decided that drunk people would like to play what is essentially the Hidden Picture puzzle from Highlights magazine. And they were right, because these things were EVERYWHERE.

ANYWAYS, that's the entire game. It's a series of still screens wherein you need to find all the hidden items on your 'clue' list. Then these clues will lead to Dr. Chaos. Though I'm not sure how a spoon, a housefly, or three alien heads are going to lead to the mad doctor's arrest. Also, can I just say here that his henchmen seem more like mental patients than hardened criminals? Especially the ditz who steals art, alters it... and then puts it back? Seriously, you're just fucking with people for fun? I mean, I can respect that, but on the master criminal scale, vandalism seems pretty low. I mean, as had been proven, you could accomplish the same thing with a can of soup. What I'm trying to say is the story is ridiculous, and only serves a a flimsy excuse for you to be jet-setting around the world.

The actual game I find charming and enjoyable. Yes, the Hidden Picture section was always my favorite while waiting for the dentist or doctor, and a video game version of such an activity is right up my alley. The graphics are actually not too shabby, though considering very little actually moves, I would hope so. I like the different, cluttered environments. One of my hobbies is thrifting, and a lot of the scenes remind me of some of the better flea markets I've been to; cozy corners filled with all kinds of treasures, except these corners are in Russia or something. The music is weirdly appealing to me as well, reminding me heavily of late 90s PC MIDI synths, which any look at my upload content should tell you I love.

Even though it didn't turn out to be what I expected, I've got a soft spot for Interpol, it's stupidity and all. Ultimately, though, it's a puzzle game, and a pretty easy one at that. I think most people would find it an amusing brain teaser for the first few levels, but drop it as a whole long before finishing the game. But hey, I know this one's available on streaming, so give it a shot. Maybe I'm wrong.

Final thoughts? First, I realized you can actually play along with me on this one, so have fun shouting at the screen when I can't spot something that's obvious. Secondly, that Hammer dude looks like the guy from Hot Fuzz who says 'Yarp' all the time. And thirdly, I feel like Tek Games specialized in phone games, and that Interpol was originally one of those. In the later stages, the PS3's PSN store was positively flooded with phone games, so I'm somewhat surprised that this one came out as long ago as it did. That's all.

3/10
